rights: Textbook records remain internal evidence; no original textbook question is made learner-displayable. Held originals remain internal and excluded from design anchors.
coverage_limits: Search is targeted to the 22 named gaps and plausible chapter/exercise candidates. It does not certify a new exhaustive reread of both books or prove absolute absence for the remaining negative search. Per-item DD labels were not edited and were not the candidate filter.

parts.reason: Take logs of the two exponential powers, use the power law, rearrange to y=mx and identify the constant logarithm ratio. Source m is rounded at its final requested precision; the exam retains that ratio exactly. The proof decisions and linear response are the same.

parts.search_notes: Searched logarithm-equation and nonlinear-substitution exercises directly: Goldie2B equations; YM9 Try10/25 leads, Exercise9 and Revision9. No exact rational-log reciprocal equation was located. Goldie2B10(ii) is the closest full repeated-quantity quadratic with explicit different domain/recovery decisions.
parts.reason: Both turn a repeated nonlinear quantity into a quadratic and recover original-variable solutions. The source quantity 5^x must be positive, so it rejects a negative quadratic root before logarithmic recovery; the exam quantity log y can have either sign, while its original denominator excludes y=1 and arguments require y>0. Those different admissibility and recovery decisions make a mixed branch, not a claim that their expressions are interchangeable.

parts.reason: Both use a logarithm power law and linearity to deduce a new definite integral from the earlier one, without computing a new primitive. The exam additionally recognises x^2-4x+4=(x-2)^2 and scales an approximation, while the source directly presents ln(x^3) and rescales an exact value. The unselected earlier geometric derivation is context.

parts.search_notes: Direct discovery in Goldie chapter3 reciprocal signs/graph tasks and YM chapter4 graph-deduction section, Exercise4.2, plus chapter8 shared graphs. Closest rejected: YM Example16(f) and Exercise8 Q19(e) compare heights; Goldie3A6(i) decides simultaneous signs from quadrants rather than a supplied pair of graphs/product. These are supporting concepts, not a full counterpart. Native pages listed in the reading records; bounded search leaves a visible gap.
parts.reason: Both read solution intervals from a supplied pair of graphs. The selected source part f tests vertical ordering f(x)≥g(x); the exam tests whether the curves have matching signs, f(x)g(x)>0, relative to the x-axis. This changed predicate and strict endpoints are a structural branch with mixed difficulty, not a same-type match. The root reread resolves the initial no-full-counterpart search conclusion consistently with B.1; it does not imply the exact product-sign task is printed in the book.

closest_items_rejected.reason: Reads the interval where the first graph is above the second: f>=g. The target combines two individual signs for fg>0; their height-order intervals do not answer that predicate.
Uses shared quadratic/modulus graphs for f>g, comparing heights. It does not identify intervals with two equal signs and exclude their zeros.
Finds angles where all reciprocal ratios are positive from quadrant signs. It provides supporting sign logic, not a supplied two-graph product-sign interval task.

previous_search_conclusion_r7.reason: The closest shared-graph textbook tasks compare heights f>=g or count intersections. The exam asks where the product is positive, requiring combining the separate signs on either side of each zero. That is not the same predicate; no full product-sign interval counterpart was found in this direct search.
